contexts.finding: PV activation suppresses population cycle markers and PV inhibition increases them; tested SST/VIP manipulations retain nulls. Conditional gamma2 deletion changes early activation and later clone composition. Isolation retains an EdU difference under PV activation, while MCM2 housing contrasts are nonsignificant. Full feedback closure and exclusive mediation remain unresolved.
limitations: Adult mouse preparations use nestin-GFP, PV/SST/VIP-Cre and nestin-CreERT2;Z/EG lines with gamma2-floxed or control alleles. Sex and a complete group-specific animal manifest are not reported. Tamoxifen is a single 62 mg/kg intraperitoneal dose at 6-10 weeks. The Methods require at least four weeks after AAV surgery; schematic week labels do not supply exact ages for every animal.

Acute 300-micrometre slices were recorded at 32-34 degrees C, with RGL voltage clamp at -65 mV and 5 mM kynurenic acid. The internal solution is ambiguously printed as 135 mM CsCl gluconate. Clamp-current sign does not directly identify native membrane polarization, spiking or cell-cycle entry.

Main text, Online Methods and Supplementary Figure 1 print 200 mM for focal GABA/muscimol application; no micromolar substitution is made. Etomidate is 100 nM in the main text/Figure 1 but 10 micromolar in Methods. The etomidate dose remains unresolved, and pharmacological sensitivity does not establish receptor stoichiometry.

Population experiments use five consecutive days of stimulation, eight hours per day: ChR2 blue light at 472 nm, 5-ms pulses at 8 Hz for 30 seconds every five minutes, or continuous 593-nm eNpHR light. AAV volume, delivered light power and a full opsin-negative illumination control are not reported. No-light sham comparisons include the effects of the complete light protocol.

On day five, EdU is injected intraperitoneally at 41.1 mg/kg six times, two hours apart, with collection two hours after the last injection. Repeated injections are not independent replicates. EdU incorporation and MCM2 expression are cycle-related endpoints, not counts of completed neuronal differentiation, integrated neurons or an instantaneous birth rate.

Population scoring uses 40-micrometre sections, every sixth section, and nestin-positive inverted-Y morphology over an EdU- or MCM2-positive nucleus. Optogenetic counts are limited to one millimetre anterior and posterior to the injection. Densities per cubic millimetre and the MCM2-positive fraction have distinct denominators. Analyses are described as blinded; random assignment, raw unit records and multiplicity-adjusted tests are not supplied.

At two and seven days after induction, one GFP-positive RGL is classified as a quiescent clone and two or more nuclei as an activated clone. These are fixed-tissue, spatially assigned clones using a referenced method, not live observations of every division or independently verified common ancestry. Supplementary Figure 2d plots one dentate gyrus per dot; hemispheres and clones cannot automatically be treated as independent animals.

Gamma2 immunostaining is shown in RGLs, but Supplementary Figure 2f electrophysiology tests GFP-positive neurons at thirty days, not RGLs. Its seven-of-ten cKO response pattern is not a measured RGL deletion efficiency. Recombination can persist in descendants, so later survival or differentiation may contribute to clone composition.

Thirty-day Figure 3f and Supplementary Figure 3e use incompletely reconciled clone denominators: the supplementary pie categories omit single-R and no-R classes. N includes intermediate progenitors or neurons, not exclusively mature neurons. Exact class percentages must not be pooled or converted to transition probabilities.

The population diazepam protocol is 5 mg/kg intraperitoneally once daily for five days. The clonal drug comparison instead uses six daily doses after tamoxifen and analysis at seven days. Diazepam is systemic. Pairwise drug responses or nulls without a reported genotype-by-drug interaction do not isolate an exclusive cell-autonomous mediator.

Social isolation starts immediately after weaning and lasts at least six weeks before labeling. The two housing conditions are crossed with light versus sham; this is not a selective learning manipulation. PV activity and extracellular GABA are not measured as the intervening response to isolation in the same animals.

Figure 5c retains higher EdU-positive RGL density in isolated versus group-housed animals under PV light stimulation (reported P < 0.05). In that same housing comparison, MCM2-positive density and fraction are nonsignificant (P > 0.1). These endpoints do not support complete abolition of the isolation effect or equivalence; the light-treated group is also distinct from the untreated group-housed baseline.

Figure 4 population comparisons use three or four animals per condition; Figure 5c uses four. Reported Student t-tests do not provide an equivalence margin, complete unit manifest or a formal factorial interaction. SST/VIP nulls apply to the tested lines, protocols and readouts, not all possible interneuron functions.

No matched experiment follows physiological circuit demand through PV signaling, RGL division, newborn-neuron survival and functional integration to restoration of circuit output. Supplementary Figure 8 imports schematic connectivity proportions, not measured weights. A reported reconstruction covering over 200 RGLs is spatial coverage, not 200 verified functional contacts or a minimum carrier count. Movie legends were read; movie files and custom reconstruction code were not replayed.

All six main PDF pages, Figures 1-5, Online Methods and all nine supplementary PDF pages with Figures 1-8 and Movie 1-3 legends were reviewed. Raw animal-level data, microscopy, recordings, movie files and analysis code were not obtained or independently reproduced.

contexts.correctionCheck: PubMed/PMC metadata and exact-DOI correction searches checked on 13 September 2026; no resolving notice identified. This is not exhaustive notice surveillance. Publication dated 11 April 2007.
contexts.finding: Selected peri-infarct samples show increased spine formation and altered morphology after photothrombosis. Recovery cohorts, optical readouts and spatial comparisons constrain injury-associated remodeling without proving behavioral restoration or a unique construction mechanism.
limitations: Adult male C57BL6 YFP-H mice were approximately 2.5-7 months old. Layer 5 neuronal apical tufts were sampled within the superficial 100 micrometers, typically 100-500 micrometers from the posterior-medial infarct edge; this is selected surviving cortex, not the whole injured brain.

Main scientific text, Materials and Methods, and Figures 1-5 with captions are reviewed. Supplemental Figures 1-2 were not obtained or read. Animal-identified image stacks, custom IgorPro routines and the allocation/exclusion manifest were not obtained; no imaging or biological experiment was independently reproduced.

Photothrombosis used Rose Bengal 100 milligrams per kilogram intraperitoneally and 532-nanometer illumination, 17 milliwatts for fifteen minutes, under ketamine-xylazine. Sham controls omitted either dye or illumination. Per-assay sham composition, random allocation and group-specific age distributions are not supplied in the reviewed account.

Imaging under urethane was acute: hourly stacks over six, occasionally seven hours, after a one-, two- or six-week recovery interval, followed by terminal histology. Separate cohorts do not trace the same spine or dendritic arbor continuously from before injury through six weeks.

Only laterally projecting spines were scored. New spines had to protrude at least four pixels, approximately 0.55 micrometers, and remain present at the six-hour endpoint. Transient events, filopodium conversions, shifted segments and poor-quality images were excluded. The assay is not a census of all spine births, losses or synapses.

Turnover is reported as a percentage of the counted spine population over the imaging session; raw animal-level numerator/denominator assignments are unavailable. Spine density is a count per ten micrometers of dendrite. Neither measure is a neuron birth rate, a universal hourly turnover constant or a calibrated graph weight.

Turnover scoring was blinded to experimental condition, but movement, abnormal breathing and image deterioration could exclude experiments; exclusion counts and animal identifiers are not supplied. Axial optical resolution was about 5.3 micrometers, much poorer than lateral resolution, and six spine-appearance cases were pooled across animals for shaft-fluorescence controls.

Spine morphology and adjacent sensory-evoked reflectance do not measure the functional efficacy of each new synapse, selective memory content or behavioral recovery. The Discussion explicitly leaves the causal link between increased formation and recovered function unestablished.

The main text gives a 0.14 percent control formation mean and 1.37, 0.93 and 0.75 percent poststroke means. The abstract describes a five- to eight-fold peak increase; these rounded quantities do not define one exact fold estimate. Retain the reported assay means without calibrating a universal multiplier.

The six-week density cohort reports five mice versus six controls but t(8)=1.43, P=0.09. The three-mouse near/far comparison reports t(3)=4.87, P<0.01 for formation and t(3)=1.92, P=0.08 for elimination. Sidedness and statistical units need resolution before numerical reproduction; these degrees of freedom do not establish an ordinary paired three-mouse test.

Orientation uses projected 15-30 micrometer segments, eighteen ten-degree bins, and three mice per group, with the infarct placed at a common reference position. Reported F(17,17) tests concern bin-distribution variance; bins are not independent mice and this is not an animal-level circular-statistical reconstruction.

The authors consider mechanical distortion during tissue loss and scar formation as well as growth and retraction. Projected dendrite-vessel alignment does not isolate shared guidance, establish physical contact or prove an optimal generative network geometry.

Texas Red dextran labels plasma. Capillary velocity in micrometers per second is distinct from volumetric perfusion; fluorescent vessel volume fraction is distinct from vessel number, connectivity and selectively demonstrated angiogenesis. The vascular cohort totals fourteen animals but per-timepoint assignments and segmentation routines remain unresolved.

The near/far spine comparison uses approximately 0.33 versus 1.65 millimeters from the infarct edge at two weeks. This is different from the orientation comparison of less than 250 versus 500-800 micrometers at six weeks. Restricted ipsilateral sampling does not establish absence of remodeling elsewhere.

Nonsignificant outcomes are not equivalence or full recovery. Photothrombosis does not permit controlled reperfusion, and the paper does not directly establish the same time course in other stroke models, traumatic injury or humans.
